rules.rule: Check for urgent sexual assault/rape conditions
rules.problem: Correct type and trigger (sexual assault OR rape); check_for lists exactly the four red-box criteria plus sex to evaluate the 5-day/3-day window. 'Injuries needing attention' is encoded as any traumatic injury (see c006).

rules.rule: Urgent: sexual assault/rape with urgent features
rules.problem: Urgent level is justified by 'Give urgent attention' and the or-structure (sex-specific time window | pregnant | injury | suicidal/overdose/self harm) matches the page. But (1) 'Traumatic injury' is broader than 'injuries needing attention', so almost any assault with a minor injury triggers Urgent; (2) the time window depends on the assault/rape finding's onset — the briefing says onset is captured when the finding is recorded, so unless the nurse back-dates onset to the assault date, the 5/3-day clause will always be true at presentation and every assault becomes Urgent.

summary: All 24 claims cite the right red-box text and use existing SNOMED concepts; the priority rule's structure, sex-specific 5/3-day windows and Urgent level match the page. The most consequential issue is that the time window relies on the assault finding's onset, which defaults to recording time, so it will likely fire for every presentation; secondarily, 'Traumatic injury' over-captures 'injuries needing attention'. No diagnosis rules are present for the page's 'Suspect sexual assault/rape' definitions, which is defensible since these are events rather than diagnoses.
